newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: COLOMBIAN FOOD GIANT EYES REGIONAL EXPANSION.
newsitem.headline: COLOMBIAN FOOD GIANT EYES REGIONAL EXPANSION.

text.p: Colombia's largest food manufacturer Alimenticias Noel announced Wednesday a $150 million plan for further expansion in Latin America.

The Medellin-based manufacturer, part of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno industrial conglomerate, said it was looking to sign deals with companies in Venezuela and Mexico and wanted to open new distribution centers in Peru, Ecuador, Panama and the United States.

Noel chairman Rafael Mario Villa said the company was considering issuing American Depository Receipts (ADRs) and was also looking at the possibility of reinvesting a greater proportion of its profits or issuing fixed term bonds.
"Any company that thinks only about the local market is wasting its time...we must look at global opportunities," Villa told press conference in Bogota.
"We're looking at the requirements (for an ADR issue) and its very probable that we will qualify," he added.
Noel, whose business is based on the manufacture of cookies, candy and meat products, began eyeing the wider regional marketplace three years ago and has already invested $145 million in expansion.
It owns a food processing plant in Venezuela, known as Industrias Alimenticias Noel de Venezuela and recently took a $27 million controlling stake in meat products manufacturer Hermo.

Noel made its entry to the Mexican market in the last quarter of last year with a joint venture to distribute its candy products via bread manufacturer Bimbo. The two companies set up a joint venture in 1994, at a cost of $36 million, to make and distribute bread in Colombia.
The Medellin food giant also has ties with Spanish firm Chupa Chups Investment Holdings BV for the distribution of candy in much of South America.
That deal includes plans to construct a manufacturing plant at an estimated cost of $23 million.
In the United States, Villa said Noel was looking to market its products to the large Hispanic population.
It already has a distribution center in Miami and is looking to open another in New York, Villa said.
